name: Stripe (stripe.com marketing, docs.stripe.com, Stripe Apps UI, Elements Appearance API; internal system Sail)
licence: Proprietary. Sail (internal design system) is not published; token names and values here come from the live docs/marketing stylesheets and public docs (Stripe Apps style guide, Elements Appearance API, accessible-color-systems post). Study structure and values only; do not reuse Sohne or marks.
bestFor: fintech, payments and infrastructure marketing with an editorial feel
developer docs that must pair with a polished marketing site
products where one saturated accent plus tinted blue-grey neutrals should signal trust
layered, coloured-shadow depth on light surfaces
avoidFor: dense dark dashboards (marketing is light-only, display weight 300)
teams without a licence for a Sohne-class grotesk (light weights depend on it)
brands needing a single consistent ink and accent across templates (stripe.com uses two inks and two purples)
small-text legibility-first contexts (body copy is weight 300 at 15-16px)

families: sohne-var (Klim Sohne variable, 1-1000; marketing, font-feature-settings "ss01"; fallback SF Pro Display / Helvetica Neue, Arial)
Source Code Pro (500, code on marketing)
docs.stripe.com: -apple-system, system-ui, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica Neue, Ubuntu (system UI stack) and Menlo/Consolas for code
Elements default: Ideal Sans, system-ui, sans-serif
typography.notes: Marketing is a light-weight display system: weight 300 for headings, body and stats, weight 400 for nav/buttons, 425 and 500 appear on the pricing template (variable axis used at non-round values). Tracking -0.02em at 32-48px, -0.025em at 56px, -0.01em at 20-34px mobile. Marketing and docs are different typographic worlds: docs use the system font stack at 14px with bold headings. Hero headline is gradient-coloured text (two stacked h1 layers measured with colours rgb(129,184,26) and rgba(0,14,255,0.5) animating). Elements Appearance API scales font sizes from --fontSizeBase in rem (fontSizeXs..3Xs / Sm..2Xl) and requires >= 16px for mobile inputs. Measured 2026-10-08 at 1440 and 390 on stripe.com, /pricing, docs.stripe.com.

color.darkMode: stripe.com marketing is light-only (body background identical under prefers-color-scheme: dark, measured 2026-10-08) but uses full-width dark-navy bands (#0d1738) for inverse sections with white-alpha text. Docs ship a dark code panel and a separate Sail theme file; docs dark-mode behaviour was not verified. Elements ships a `night` theme next to `stripe` and `flat` themes.
color.contrastNotes: Computed WCAG on white: ink #061b31 17.37:1, #0a2540 ~16:1 class, body #50617a 6.30:1, muted #64748d 4.75:1, primary #533afd 6.19:1, #635bff 4.70:1, docs #5469d4 4.83:1 (white text on it 4.83:1). Stripe's own method (public post): Lab-based ramps tuned so any two steps 5 apart pass 4.5:1 and 4 apart pass 3:1 on any hue, including on the lightest tint of each hue; audit found no default text colour other than black met 4.5:1 before the rebuild.

spacing.base: unknown for marketing; Stripe Apps tokens 2/4/8 steps; Elements spacingUnit default 2px (everything derives from it). Notes: Stripe Apps spacing tokens: 0, xxsmall 2px, xsmall 4px, small 8px, medium 16px, large 24px, xlarge 32px, xxlarge 48px. Marketing layout measured at 1440: nav height 76px; page frame has 1px vertical grid lines at x=88 and x=1352 (1264px frame), hero content inset to x=208 (stat bar to the right), logo strip inside frame; sections 7-10 are 1232px wide. Section heights vary 560-4530px; vertical rhythm not tokenised in the stylesheet.

radius.rule: Marketing home buttons and chips are 4px (57 elements), cards 6px (38), small controls 5px; pricing template uses fully rounded 16.5px pills at 33px height; docs use 4px buttons, 6px inputs, 8px panels, 14px large cards. Elements default borderRadius 4px (buttonBorderRadius overrides). Two button grammars (square-ish 4px and pill) coexist on stripe.com templates.

shadows: signature small: rgba(50,50,93,0.25) 0 2px 5px -1px, rgba(0,0,0,0.3) 0 1px 3px -1px (x20, pricing controls)
docs button ring: rgb(212,222,233) 0 0 0 1px (box-shadow used as border)
Elements documented focus: 0 1px 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.03), 0 3px 6px rgba(18,42,66,0.02), 0 0 0 2px var(--colorPrimary); invalid: 0 1px 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.07), 0 0 0 2px var(--colorDanger)
depth.borders: 1px hairlines in #e5edf5 and 1px vertical frame lines; docs use box-shadow rings as borders. Shadows are tinted with the blue-violet #32325d (rgb 50,50,93) so they read as part of the palette rather than grey.
depth.blur: nav bar background rgba(255,255,255,0.8) (backdrop blur not extracted, inferred); gradient hero uses large blurred radial gradients (blur radius not measured).

motion.notes: Hover feedback 100-300ms, reveal and emphasis 600-1200ms. Home page animates headline colour over 1.2s as scroll feedback and a live GDP counter (1.72881855%) as a motion element. Docs buttons: 240ms background-color/box-shadow. prefers-reduced-motion not verified.

components.stateMatrixCompleteness: Public for Elements: Appearance API exposes rules per component and state (e.g. .Input, .Input:focus, .Input--invalid, .Tab, .Tab--selected, .Label, .Block) over 3 themes (stripe, night, flat) and an `inputs` (spaced, condensed) x `labels` (auto, above, floating) matrix, ~60+ variables; for Stripe Apps components have fixed presets and limited CSS (Chips change by callbacks, not overridable). Marketing/docs component state matrices are not published.

tokenArchitecture: Sail (internal) exposes in the shipped docs CSS: ramp primitives --sail-color-{hue}-{50..900|950} each with a -rgb triplet twin for alpha compositing (e.g. --sail-color-blue-500-rgb: 84, 105, 212), semantic aliases (--sail-color-background, -background-canvas, -background-offset, -line-divider, -line-divider-medium, -line-divider-dark, -line-keyline), and hue aliasing so a theme re-points whole ramps (orange to yellow, purple to blue, blue to cyan). Components then read hashed utility vars (--s-xxxx). Public layers: Stripe Apps tokens as typed props (spacing xxsmall..xxlarge, keyline, backgroundColor, color/fill, font) so only token values are allowed; Elements three-tier theme > variables > rules with computed accessibleColorOn* variables that choose readable text for any brand colour.
distinctiveness: Light-weight Sohne (300) at display sizes with negative tracking and gradient-filled headline words; navy ink (#061b31) instead of black; one saturated purple (#533afd) over blue-tinted greys; shadows tinted with #32325d and stacked in two layers with negative spread; 1px grid-line frame around the whole page; full-bleed gradient art (the wave) behind the hero; dark-navy inverse bands; live numbers as a motion device. Generic SaaS copies the purple and the gradient but not the 300 weight, ink hue or tinted layered shadow.
weaknesses: stripe.com carries two inks (#061b31 vs #0a2540) and two purples (#533afd vs #635bff) across templates; button grammar differs (4px square vs 16.5px pill) between home and pricing
weight 300 body at 15-16px with #50617a text is thin and borderline for low-vision users
docs (system fonts, 14px, bold headings) and marketing (Sohne 300) share almost no typographic DNA
Sail is not public, so there is no component spec to copy; only values and token names are visible

hero gradient art and animated gradient text are heavy and decorative; a public secondary source reports the gradient wave was retired in a 2026 redesign, yet it was present on 2026-10-08 (variant or rollout difference not resolved)
takeaways: Build colour ramps in a perceptual space with equal lightness per step across hues, so 'N steps apart' guarantees contrast (5 apart for text, 4 apart for icons)
Keep an -rgb triplet twin of every ramp colour for alpha compositing
Tint shadows with the brand's blue-violet and stack two layers (large soft + small tight with negative spread) instead of grey single shadows
Compute accessibleColorOn* tokens (text on primary, on background, on danger) rather than asking designers to pick them
Expose theming as three tiers (theme, variables, rules) and restrict custom styling to token values to keep a high accessibility bar
Use ink and body colours with a blue-grey cast (navy ink, slate body) instead of pure black and neutral grey
Light display weight (300) works only with a high-quality grotesk and negative tracking scaled to size; do not apply 300 to body copy in a default font
Frame the page with 1px structural lines and let one art object (gradient) bleed through the frame
Re-point whole hue ramps by alias to re-theme (hue aliasing) instead of editing each token
